program_name: Strategic Communication (Master's Degree Course in Strategic Communication)
teaching_language: Fully English-taught. The IULM programme page states the course is "taught entirely in English" and lists the teaching language simply as "English"; the apply.iulm.it course record likewise gives "Study language: English". There is no Italian-taught component of the curriculum. However, the admission regulations impose a separate Italian-language obligation that is NOT an entry condition but a graduation condition: candidates who are not native Italian speakers and/or non-Italian citizens must declare their Italian level when applying and must obtain, by the end of their studies, a qualification attesting to written and oral proficiency in Italian.
campus: Milan (Milano) - IULM single campus, Via Carlo Bo 1, 20143 Milano
degree_class: LM-59 - Scienze della comunicazione pubblica, d'impresa e pubblicita (rendered on the English pages as "LM-59 - Science of public communication, business and advertising" and in the admission regulations as "LM-59 Public, Corporate and Advertising Communication Sciences")
academic_requirements:
PLACES: 100 places for a.y. 2026/2027 ("1. Number of places available for the academic year 2026/2027 - 100 places"). The programme page classifies it as a "Course with planned number of places with selective knowledge testing".

PRIOR QUALIFICATION: A first-cycle (Bachelor's) university degree, awarded or about to be awarded. Candidates must expect to graduate before the autumn session of a.y. 2025/26, i.e. before 31 December 2026. For international applicants apply.iulm.it states the entry qualification is an "Undergraduate diploma (or higher) Bachelor's degree" evaluated case by case, and the general IULM master prerequisites page requires "a relevant and coherent Bachelor's degree diploma correspondent to EQF (European Qualification Framework) Level 6 and 180 ECTS or more".

CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS (route 1 - degree class): the Bachelor's degree must belong to one of the Italian classes L-1 (Cultural heritage), L-10 (Arts), L-11 (Modern languages and cultures), L-12 (Language mediation), L-16 (Administration and organisation), L-18 (Economics and corporate management), L-19 (Education and training), L-20 (Communication), L-24 (Psychology), L-33 (Economics), L-36 (Politics and international relations), L-37 (Social sciences for cooperation, development and peace), L-40 (Sociology), or an equivalent foreign degree qualification.

CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS (route 2 - credits): candidates graduating in any other class must have acquired at least 60 CFU/ECTS in the listed scientific-disciplinary sectors: ICAR/13; IUS/07, IUS/09; L-LIN/12; SECS-P/01, P/02, P/03, P/05, P/06, P/07, P/08, P/09, P/10, P/11, P/13; SPS/01, SPS/04, SPS/07, SPS/08, SPS/09, SPS/11, SPS/12; SECS-S/01 to S/06; MAT/05, MAT/06, MAT/08, MAT/09; M-PSI/01, M-PSI/05, M-PSI/06; INF/01 - obtained in the Bachelor's degree, via single university courses, or via a university master.

EXCLUSIONS: "Applications will not be accepted from graduates from AFAM Institutes (Istituzioni di Alta Formazione Artistica, Musicale e Coreutica)." SSML (Scuole Superiori per Mediatori Linguistici) applicants are assessed individually and must e-mail a detailed exam certificate to ammissioni.magistrali@iulm.it before applying online; they may only apply after approval by the Coordinator for Master's Degree Courses.

RANKING / SELECTION CRITERIA - three distinct candidate tracks:
(a) INTERNAL graduates/undergraduates (IULM Bachelor's in Comunicazione d'impresa e relazioni pubbliche or Corporate Communication and Public Relations) applying in sessions 1-2 are ranked WITHOUT any test, on average mark (rounded to 2 decimals): session 1 requires >=90 CFU registered as of 25 Nov 2025 and average >=25/30, with later verification of 120 CFU as of 15 Feb 2026; session 2 requires >=120 CFU as of 15 Feb 2026 and average >=25/30; graduates need a pre-graduation exam average >=25/30. "A maximum total of 50 candidates will be admitted to the ranking list in the first two sessions." Internal candidates must also meet the English B2 requirement, except those from the Corporate Communication and Public Relations degree. Internal candidates who exceed the 50-place internal quota or fall below the merit threshold take the same test as external candidates. From session 3 onwards internal candidates take the same test and enter a single ranking list.
(b) EXTERNAL graduates/undergraduates: admission is by admission test score plus merit points. Merit points on Bachelor's degree grade: up to 88/110 = 0 points; 89-98/110 = 1 point; 99-110/110 = 2 points; 110/110 cum laude = 3 points. For undergraduates, merit points are based instead on the registered exam average: up to and including 25.99/30 = 0; 26/30-27.99/30 = 1; 28/30-29.99/30 = 2; 30/30 = 3. External undergraduates must have registered at least 90 CFU as of 25 Nov 2025 (session 1, with later verification of 120 CFU as of 15 Feb 2026), 120 CFU as of 15 Feb 2026 (session 2), 130 CFU as of 23 Apr 2026 (session 3), 130 CFU as of 18 Jun 2026 (session 4). "Candidates will be admitted in the ranking list up to the number of places assigned for each session." Tie-break: degree mark (graduates) or exam average (undergraduates) at application; further tie broken by date of payment of the application fee.
(c) FOREIGN graduates (holders of a foreign admission qualification, EU or non-EU, obtained in Italy or abroad): "The candidate's individual knowledge and skills will be assessed by means of a written paper (of no more than 1400 words) based on a case study assigned after the verification of the curricular requirements. The case study assesses the level of knowledge of basic communication and marketing concepts." Eligible foreign students are assigned places OUTSIDE the external-candidate ranking list in the first session, and places in the single ranking list in subsequent sessions.

ASSESSMENT OF FOREIGN QUALIFICATIONS: IULM's Admission Office evaluates all documentation, checks access requirements and confirms eligibility before the admission test. At enrolment, holders of a foreign qualification must supply the qualification in the original language with an Italian translation where required, plus authenticity verification - "a Statement of Comparability and/or CIMEA verification, or a Dichiarazione di Valore (official statement issued by the Italian diplomatic authorities), as required by the University".

DUAL DEGREE: The programme offers dual-degree routes with Cardiff Metropolitan University (UK) - Postgraduate Certificate in International Business Management - and the University of Western Australia / UWA (Perth, Australia) - Graduate Certificate of Strategic Communication. The mobility window is the second semester of the second year. IULM's published pages describe these as opportunities students "can choose" but do NOT publish separate partner-side entry criteria (GPA thresholds, partner English scores, internal selection), so any stricter Cardiff Met / UWA requirements are not captured here - see uncertainty_notes. [uncertain]

SPECIAL NEEDS: applicants with disabilities (Law 104/92), Specific Learning Disorders (Law 170/2010), ADHD or Autism must upload valid certification in PDF during online test enrolment and request accommodations by e-mail to the diversaMENTE service (diversamente@iulm.it) before the test enrolment deadline.
language_requirements:
ENGLISH - minimum CEFR B2, verified in one of four alternative ways (admission regulations, section 4 "Language requirement: English language proficiency to at least level B2"):
1. A language certificate obtained after 1 January 2024: IELTS with a score of at least 5.5; TOEFL iBT with a score of at least 87; Cambridge English with a score of at least 165.
2. A Bachelor's degree (obtained in Italy or abroad) on a course held in English.
3. Passing IULM's own Assessment Test (Oxford Placement Test), offered online at no extra cost, with a grade of at least level B2 in BOTH the Listening and Use of English sections - so IULM's own placement test fully substitutes for an external certificate.
4. Having already passed the IULM Assessment Test at B2 or above in both sections in an admissions session of a.y. 2025/26, and in any case not before 1 February 2025.
Candidates who do not meet the requirement at test registration are automatically placed on the Assessment Test list. Assessment Test dates for a.y. 2026/27: 1 December 2025 (session 1); 20 January and 25 February 2026 (session 2); 9 April and 28 April 2026 (session 3, "only if places still available or only for non-EU students"); 25 June 2026 (session 4, same condition); session 5 dates to be defined only if places remain.
For foreign candidates specifically: "Foreign applicants who are not native speakers of English are required to present international language certification attesting to their level of English language proficiency to at least level B2 before taking the admissions test; alternatively, they must pass the Assessment Test with at least level B2."
EXEMPTION: internal IULM candidates from the Corporate Communication and Public Relations Bachelor's degree are exempt from the English language requirement.

ITALIAN - not an admission requirement, but a graduation requirement. "Candidates who are not native speakers of Italian and/or non-Italian citizens are required to declare their level of knowledge of the Italian language when applying for the admissions test, and they must obtain by the end of their course of studies the required qualification attesting to written and oral proficiency in Italian." Candidates are directed to the University's published "Procedures for the assessment and acquisition of knowledge of the Italian language". The general international-prerequisites page states that for Italian-taught courses a CILS/CELI/PLIDA certificate at CEFR B2 or IULM's online Italian assessment test is required; the exact Italian level demanded for graduation from this English-taught course is not stated on the pages consulted. [uncertain]
application_deadline_eu:
Academic year 2026/2027. Applications open 11 November 2025 ("From 11 November 2025, the following categories of candidates will be able to apply for admission following the online procedure"). The overall master's registration period runs 11 November 2025 - 31 August 2026.

Five admission sessions are foreseen for Strategic Communication. Per session: [application deadline] -> [test date] -> [enrolment confirmation deadline]
- Session 1: apply by 25 November 2025 (registration for session 1 opened 11 November 2025 at 10:00 and closed 25 November 2025 at 23:59) -> test 10 December 2025 -> enrol by 15 January 2026.
- Session 2: apply by 19 February 2026 -> test 11 March 2026 -> enrol by 31 March 2026. (Merit/CFU documentation deadline for this session: 15 February 2026.)
- Session 3: apply by 23 April 2026 -> test 13 May 2026 -> enrol by 4 June 2026. Held "only if places still available or only for non-EU students". An exceptional enrolment date of 29 June 2026 also appears in the general master's enrolment calendar.
- Session 4: apply by 18 June 2026 (registration window 22 May 2026 10:00 - 18 June 2026 23:59) -> test 8 July 2026 -> enrol by 28 July 2026. Held "only if places still available or only for non-EU students".
- Session 5: registration window 30 June - 31 August 2026 with enrolment deadline 18 September 2026 in the general master's calendar; for Strategic Communication the regulations say "5th session: dates to be defined only if places still available".

IMPORTANT: for a.y. 2026/2027 Strategic Communication was ALREADY FULL before session 4 - IULM's 25 May 2026 news item states "For Marketing, Consumer Behaviour and Communication (English language course) and Strategic Communication, seats are sold out." No Strategic Communication test date was listed for session 4, and apply.iulm.it shows the 2026/27 application period as ended. In practice the last usable EU deadlines were session 3 (apply by 23 April 2026, test 13 May 2026).

Other notes: "Deadlines for sessions following the first are subject to the availability of places." "Depending on the number of admissions and the number of remaining places, the deadlines for enrolments may be shortened to allow the scrolling of the ranking list." Candidates who fail one session may re-apply for a later session without paying the EUR 110 test fee again, subject to places being available. Enrolment is confirmed only on payment of the first instalment. Candidates without a degree certificate yet are enrolled "conditionally" and must communicate the degree date and grade and upload the certificate no later than 31 December 2026, failing which the enrolment is annulled with no refund. Teaching for a.y. 2026/27 starts 21 September 2026.
application_deadline_non_eu:
Non-EU applicants residing abroad apply through the dedicated international platform apply.iulm.it, not through the standard Italian online procedure. The international procedure page states: "Non-EU applicants living abroad can submit their application on apply.iulm.it, subject to availability of places for the two-year master degree course in which they are interested, by the end of April." So the effective non-EU application cut-off for a.y. 2026/2027 was the end of April 2026.

Steps: (1) submit the application with all required documents on apply.iulm.it; (2) pay the application fee (apply.iulm.it lists "Application fee EUR 60 one-time"; the IULM admission regulations separately set the admission test fee at EUR 110, and for foreign candidates admitted to the remote admissions test "the enrolment fee is reduced by 50%, and may be waived if the test is carried out through a Recruiting Agent"); (3) eligibility evaluation, approximately 15 working days; (4) sit the admission test online (for foreign-qualification holders, the written case-study paper of max 1400 words); (5) enrol via the University's Online Services; (6) pay the tuition deposit / first instalment to secure the place.

VISA / PRE-ENROLMENT: admitted non-EU students must lodge the pre-enrolment request for a study visa with the Italian consular authorities. IULM instructs applicants to "submit a student visa application via Universitaly platform from March to the end of May", and apply.iulm.it adds: "Admitted students must submit pre-enrolment request for student visa to the Italian consular authorities. For more details on the procedure and any updates, visit: www.studiare-in-italia.it/studentistranieri/."

FINAL ENROLMENT CUT-OFF FOR FOREIGN-QUALIFICATION HOLDERS: "Students holding a foreign qualification are required to complete the enrolment process no later than 31 January 2027 by submitting all documentation required for this purpose, including: a Type D study visa (where required); their tax code (codice fiscale); the admission qualification in the original language together with an Italian translation (where required); and documentation verifying the authenticity of the qualification, such as a Statement of Comparability and/or CIMEA verification, or a Dichiarazione di Valore." Failure to comply by 31 January 2027 annuls the 2026/27 enrolment ex officio with no refund of fees already paid.

REFUNDS: the first instalment is non-refundable, with one exception - it "can be refunded solely and exclusively on production of official documentation from the relevant Consulate certifying failure to obtain a study visa."

STATUS FOR 2026/2027: closed. apply.iulm.it displays for the 2026/27 intake: "Application period has ended" with the note "Unfortunately, applications for the upcoming academic year 2026/2027 are closed since we reached full capacity for this programme." Sessions 3 and 4 were in any case flagged in the regulations as running "only if places still available or only for non-EU students", i.e. late sessions are reserved primarily for non-EU candidates.

entry_exam_or_test:
Restricted-access programme with a selective admission test. Fee: EUR 110, "not refundable under any circumstances (with the exception of failure to take the test due to the exhaustion of available places or at the behest of the University's governing bodies)". All candidates must register and pay, including those admitted directly. Non-payment, or payment after the session deadline, bars admission to the test. For foreign candidates admitted to the remote test the enrolment fee is reduced by 50% and may be waived if the test is taken through a Recruiting Agent.

FORMAT - main test: "The admissions test consists of an oral test held in English". "The tests will be carried out online." The assessment commissions comprise at least two members besides the candidate. Set reading for preparation: Invernizzi E., Romenti S. (2023), "Conceptual and Operational Evolution of PR and Corporate Communication", in Invernizzi E., Romenti S. (eds), Corporate Communication and Public Relations Handbook, McGraw-Hill (the chapter is made available to candidates by the University). The test duration is not published. [uncertain]

FORMAT - foreign graduates: instead of the oral test, holders of a foreign admission qualification are assessed "by means of a written paper (of no more than 1400 words) based on a case study assigned after the verification of the curricular requirements. The case study assesses the level of knowledge of basic communication and marketing concepts."

PRELIMINARY ENGLISH TEST: candidates without an accepted B2 certificate or an English-taught Bachelor's are automatically scheduled for the free online Assessment Test (Oxford Placement Test), which must be passed at B2 or above in both the Listening and Use of English sections. Dates: 1 Dec 2025; 20 Jan and 25 Feb 2026; 9 Apr and 28 Apr 2026; 25 Jun 2026; session 5 to be defined. (The general IULM master's calendar also lists English assessment dates of 27 May 2026 and 4 September 2026.)

TEST DATES FOR STRATEGIC COMMUNICATION, a.y. 2026/2027: session 1 - 10 December 2025; session 2 - 11 March 2026; session 3 - 13 May 2026 (only if places still available or only for non-EU students); session 4 - 8 July 2026 (only if places still available or only for non-EU students); session 5 - to be defined only if places remain. In practice no session-4 test was held for this programme because seats were sold out. "The dates of the tests already scheduled are subject to changes, which will be communicated to the candidates in advance."

SCORING: the test result is combined with merit points (0-3) derived from the Bachelor's degree grade (graduates) or registered exam average (undergraduates); candidates enter a ranking list and are admitted up to the number of places assigned to each session. Candidates who fail a session may re-sit in a later session without paying the fee again, subject to availability of places. There is no separate interview stage for this programme (unlike IULM's Hospitality and Tourism Management, which runs a two-stage written plus oral test).

uncertainty_notes:
YEAR COVERED: All figures are for academic year 2026/2027, taken from the English-language admission regulations "Modalita ammissione LM STRATEGIC 2026_2027_ENG.pdf" (Faculty Board meeting 13/10/2025, revised Faculty Board meeting 3/3/2026) and the 2026/2027 tuition regulations (Rector's Decree no. 21472 of 27 November 2025). No 2025/2026 fallback was needed.

PROGRAMME REPORTED FULL/CLOSED BEFORE THE FINAL SESSION - CONFIRMED. IULM's news item of 25 May 2026 announcing the fourth test session states: "For Marketing, Consumer Behaviour and Communication (English language course) and Strategic Communication, seats are sold out." No Strategic Communication test date appears in the session-4 list, and apply.iulm.it shows the 2026/27 application period as ended with the note that applications "are closed since we reached full capacity for this programme". Practical consequence: although the regulations schedule sessions up to a possible fifth, the 100 places were exhausted by session 3 (test 13 May 2026, apply by 23 April 2026). Applicants should treat the November-to-April window as the real one and apply in session 1 or 2. Note also that the regulations already flag sessions 3 and 4 as running "only if places still available or only for non-EU students".

DUAL DEGREE - PARTNER REQUIREMENTS NOT PUBLISHED BY IULM. IULM confirms two dual-degree routes: a Postgraduate Certificate in International Business Management at Cardiff Metropolitan University (UK) and a Graduate Certificate of Strategic Communication at UWA / University of Western Australia (Perth), taken in the second semester of the second year. However, none of the accessible iulm.it / iulm.com / apply.iulm.it / openday.iulm.it pages publishes the partner-side selection criteria - no minimum IULM GPA, no internal quota for the dual-degree places, no partner-specific English-score threshold (Cardiff Met and UWA typically require higher IELTS than IULM's 5.5, but that could not be confirmed from an IULM source and is therefore NOT asserted here), no partner tuition or additional fee, and no separate application deadline for the mobility. The openday.iulm.it page refers to "three Dual Degree opportunities" while the main programme page names two certificates at two universities - this discrepancy is unresolved. Prospective students must contact IULM (admission@iulm.it / ammissioni.magistrali@iulm.it) for the dual-degree selection rules. Note also that apply.iulm.it lists the international course record under the title "MA Strategic Communication - Dual Degree", which suggests the dual-degree route is how the programme is marketed to international applicants, but the admission regulations make no distinction between a dual-degree and a standard track at the admission stage.

ADMISSION TEST DURATION NOT PUBLISHED. The regulations specify the format (an online oral test in English for Italian-qualification candidates; a written case-study paper of max 1400 words for foreign-qualification holders) and the single set reading, but give no duration for either. The number of questions/topics beyond the assigned chapter is likewise not published.

ITALIAN-LANGUAGE GRADUATION REQUIREMENT NOT QUANTIFIED. The regulations require non-native-Italian speakers to obtain "by the end of their course of studies the required qualification attesting to written and oral proficiency in Italian" and refer to a separate document, "Procedures for the assessment and acquisition of knowledge of the Italian language", which was not retrieved. The CEFR level and the accepted certificates for that graduation requirement are therefore unknown; the B2 CILS/CELI/PLIDA standard cited on the general international-prerequisites page applies expressly to Italian-taught programmes, not necessarily to this English-taught one.

FEE FIGURES. The tuition_or_fees_link PDF applies to students whose family resides abroad (single contribution band): EUR 10,806 total for a first-year master's student (EUR 2,000 first instalment + EUR 146 regional tax advance, EUR 5,300 + EUR 60 due by 14/12/2026, EUR 3,300 due by 31/03/2027), matching the EUR 10,806 shown on apply.iulm.it. A reduced band of EUR 4,646 applies to students from developing countries listed in Ministerial Decree no. 166/2025. Students assessed on Italian ISEE pay according to the separate general fee regulations, which were not extracted here. The programme registration page still links the 2025/2026 fee summary alongside the 2026/2027 one.

OTHER. The registration page (".../strategic-communication/iscrizioni") displays only sessions 2 and 3 in its countdown widget; the full five-session calendar comes from the admission regulations PDF and the general master's enrolment page, which lists a fifth session window of 30 June - 31 August 2026 with an 18 September 2026 enrolment deadline and an exceptional 29 June 2026 enrolment date - these general dates are not repeated in the Strategic Communication regulations, which say only "5th session: dates to be defined only if places still available". The apply.iulm.it page could not be retrieved by WebFetch (HTTP 403) and was read via direct HTTP request instead; its content is quoted as displayed on 6 September 2026.
